newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's deputy PM pushes for more toilet talk.
newsitem.headline: Australia's deputy PM pushes for more toilet talk.

text.p: Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer wants to flush out political views in the new parliament house by blocking up the plumbing in politicians' private toilets.
Fischer says the flow of communication has slowed to a trickle in the absence of the communal troughs which were a feature of the old parliament house, vacated in 1988.
At the launch of a book of humorous political anecdotes on Monday, Fischer bemoaned the fact that humour has become more highbrow since it has been taken from the toilets to the tearoom.

"There is no doubt in my mind that the reason there is less humour in the new parliament house is a design fault which would be greatly helped if we turned off all the plumbing in individual members' and senators' suites," Fischer said.
This would aid the democratic process by re-establishing the rapport created by "informal" contact, which is necessary for bipartisan decision making, Fischer said.
Former prime minister Gough Whitlam is in full agreement with Fischer, acknowledging that great communication took place in the "loos" of old parliament house.
Australia's luxurious A$1.1 billion (US$740 million) parliament house gives each MP their own toilet suite, unlike the overcrowded 70-year-old building it replaced.
